institution: Kottayam district AMR laboratory (hub General Hospital Kottayam and 26 spoke hospitals), KARS-Net district antibiogram, Department of Health Services, Kerala
citation: Kerala Antimicrobial Resistance Strategic Action Plan (KARSAP), Department of Health Services, Kerala. District Antibiogram: Alappuzha, Kottayam, Pathanamthitta, Thrissur and Thiruvananthapuram. Chapter: District Antibiogram Kottayam, Antibiogram 2023-2024 (1 January 2023 to 31 December 2024), compiled by Dr Anupama Rajani, District Clinical Microbiologist, District AMR Lab, GH Kottayam. Thiruvananthapuram: Department of Health Services, Kerala.
reporting: Percent resistant with number tested and number resistant, by organism and specimen (pus swabs and aspirates, urine), hub plus spokes, all locations pooled; spoke-only tables printed separately; percentages not computed when fewer than 30 isolates.
method: Conventional disc diffusion; WHONET; CLSI interpretive criteria; one result per patient per specimen type and pathogen (1343 unique-patient isolates, 2023 to 2024).

verification.note: Tables 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 13 and 15 read from the PDF text layer and compared value by value with the pages rendered at scale 2.2 (Table 10 row alignment and the misprinted tested counts checked on the image); every printed percentage recomputed from its printed counts. Page numbers are 1-based PDF pages of the five-district compilation.

notes: District antibiogram of secondary and primary care facilities: District AMR Lab at General Hospital Kottayam (hub) and 26 spoke institutions (general and taluk hospitals, community, family and primary health centres), 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2024 (two years), from the KARSAP compilation of five district antibiograms. All figures are percent resistant. 78% of isolates were from outpatients, 21% inpatients and under 1% ICU; tables pool all locations. Pus swabs and aspirates are recorded as pus. Blood yielded 3 priority isolates and stool 1 (counts only).
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: the 40-cell seeded sample was read blind from the page images (scale 2.5), then all 80 cells, their numbers tested, all 9 row n values and all 49 counts (Table 2 page 42, location table page 44) were re-read and compared: 0 transcription errors; organism and specimen correct on every row; the counts agree across the specimen and location tables.

Conflicts confirmed accurate: E. coli urine amoxicillin-clavulanate and cefuroxime are both printed as 626 resistant of 616 tested with 53% (checked on a scale-5 crop of page 48; 53% of 616 would be 326). Also confirmed as printed: Klebsiella pus tested counts 2710 (ciprofloxacin) and 2309 (co-trimoxazole), whose number tested is rightly left out; the page 44 narrative (30% methicillin, 68% erythromycin resistance in pus) against Table 4 (24% and 69%), with page 54 also giving 24% MRSA in pus.
